paper_metadata.title: Comparative Study of Quantum-Circuit Scalability in a Financial Problem

summary: The paper analyzes how the number of two‑qubit gates in a Quantum Amplitude Estimation circuit for a simplified Treasury‑bill pricing model scales with evaluation qubits when compiled to different architectures. For 1–19 evaluation qubits, the fitted scaling is n² for IonQ trapped‑ion hardware and n²+n for an ideal superconducting device, while realistic IBM devices show higher costs (≈2.1n²−4.7n+6.8 for Tokyo and ≈3.5n²−12.8n+22.3 for Cairo), implying roughly a 2–3× reduction in two‑qubit gates for ion‑trap systems due to all‑to‑all connectivity.

experiments.description: Scalability study of quantum amplitude estimation for Treasury Bill expectation-value estimation, comparing two-qubit gate requirements when the same QAE circuit is mapped to IBM superconducting devices versus IonQ trapped-ion devices across 1 to 19 evaluation qubits.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Amplitude Estimation (QAE) for simplified Treasury Bill expectation-value estimation
algorithm.parameter_initialization: State preparation via A gate / RY(θ) with θ = 2 sin^-1(sqrt(p)); no variational optimization

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Binary outcome values Vlow=$0 and Vhigh=$1 are encoded on a single objective qubit; probability p is loaded via an RY(θ) rotation. Evaluation qubits control repeated applications of Q in the QAE/QPE subroutine.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the expectation value V = (1-p)Vlow + pVhigh for a simplified Treasury Bill model; equivalently estimate p and compute V classically.

problem_instance.description: Simplified Treasury Bill (zero-coupon bond) expectation-value estimation problem used as a finance example for QAE scalability.

dataset_specification.description: Toy single-period binomial model with Vlow and Vhigh; example probability p=0.2 in the illustrative circuit.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: No dataset preprocessing; probability p is directly encoded into the circuit via rotation angle θ = 2 sin^-1(sqrt(p)).
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Circuit transpilation and two-qubit gate counting across 1 to 19 evaluation qubits; repeated transpilation runs for IBM real devices due to routing variability; polynomial fits reported for gate-count scaling.

hardware.device_name: Qiskit transpiled backends (IBM Yorktown, Tokyo, Cairo topologies) and hypothetical 'IBM ideal' connectivity model

implementation_details.transpilation_target: IBM backends and IonQ-style trapped-ion gate decomposition; Qiskit transpile used for backend-specific circuit generation

transpilation_settings.routing_method: Qiskit transpile / SABRE mentioned as a possible mapper

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: None beyond analytical mapping of p to rotation angle and backend-specific transpilation.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Most probable measurement outcome is converted back to an estimated probability and then to bond value classically.

speedup_claims.conditions: QAE amplitude estimation with M samples / queries
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the convergence rate improvement is O(M^-1) versus O(M^-1/2), and success probability is at least 8/pi^2.

speedup_claims.conditions: Across 1 to 19 evaluation qubits; comparing IonQ trapped-ion to IBM superconducting mappings
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a circuit-complexity reduction, not a runtime benchmark.

complexity_analysis.constant_factor_quantum: Success probability at least 8/pi^2; two to three factor reduction in two-qubit gates on IonQ vs superconducting devices reported

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not estimated; paper analyzes gate-count scaling only
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Requires large‑scale fault‑tolerant QAE circuits with many evaluation qubits; current analysis only examines up to 19 evaluation qubits and counts two‑qubit gates after transpilation.
limiting_factors: Only circuit gate-count scaling studied; no runtime or hardware execution results
Quadratic quantum speedup (QAE vs Monte Carlo) insufficient under Hoefler constant‑factor analysis
Two‑qubit gate overhead and routing complexity on superconducting hardware

notes: num_qubits is not given as a single total register size for the main scalability study; the paper reports 1 to 19 evaluation qubits and a single objective qubit, so total qubits are inferred as evaluation_qubits + 1 when needed.

hardware.type is set to real_qpu_superconducting because the paper explicitly analyzes IBM superconducting devices; IonQ trapped-ion results are also discussed in the same experiment, but the primary hardware class is superconducting for the IBM side.
Authors discuss theoretical quadratic speedup of QAE over classical Monte Carlo but do not demonstrate runtime advantage.
The work evaluates two‑qubit gate scaling after transpilation rather than solving a practical pricing problem.

experiments.description: IonQ trapped-ion implementation of the same QAE Treasury Bill circuit, emphasizing native-gate decomposition and all-to-all connectivity to reduce two-qubit gate overhead relative to IBM superconducting devices.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Amplitude Estimation (QAE) mapped to trapped-ion native gates
algorithm.parameter_initialization: State preparation via RY(θ) with θ = 2 sin^-1(sqrt(p)); no variational optimization

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Same simplified Treasury Bill encoding as exp_1; objective qubit encodes Vlow/Vhigh and evaluation qubits control Q operations.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the expectation value V = (1-p)Vlow + pVhigh.

problem_instance.description: Same simplified Treasury Bill expectation-value estimation problem, compiled to IonQ trapped-ion native gates.

dataset_specification.description: Toy single-period binomial model; example p=0.2.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: None; direct angle encoding of p.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Two-qubit gate counts measured after mapping the QAE circuit to IonQ native gates for 1 to 19 evaluation qubits; polynomial fit reported.

hardware.device_name: IonQ trapped‑ion architecture model (MS/RXX native gate decomposition analyzed via transpilation)

implementation_details.transpilation_target: IonQ trapped-ion native decomposition using RX, RY, RZ, and RXX/MS-style entangling gates
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: None beyond analytical mapping of p to θ.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Classical conversion of the most probable measured bitstring to the estimated probability/value.

speedup_claims.conditions: QAE on trapped-ion hardware with all-to-all connectivity
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper emphasizes reduced two-qubit-gate overhead relative to superconducting devices, not a direct runtime speedup measurement.

speedup_claims.factor: 2x-3x reduction in two-qubit gates relative to superconducting devices
speedup_claims.conditions: Same QAE circuit mapped to IonQ native gates
speedup_claims.caveats: The reduction is reported from gate-count scaling and example circuits.

complexity_analysis.constant_factor_quantum: Reported two to three factor reduction in two-qubit gates relative to superconducting devices

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Large‑scale trapped‑ion QAE circuits with many logical qubits and error‑corrected MS‑type entangling gates.
limiting_factors: Architecture comparison limited to theoretical gate counts
No hardware execution or performance benchmark
Problem instance is a toy single‑period T‑Bill model

notes: IonQ hardware is discussed as a separate device class within the same scalability experiment; total qubit count is inferred from the number of evaluation qubits plus one objective qubit when needed.
IonQ advantage discussed only in terms of lower two‑qubit gate counts due to all‑to‑all connectivity, not computational advantage over classical algorithms.
